narrativeProgression.description: Morton Klein outlines his criticisms of the Conference of Presidents and other Jewish organizations, arguing they are driven by leftist ideology and fear rather than authentic pro-Israel sentiment.
Morton Klein identifies J Street, New Israel Fund, T'ruah, and the Reform movement as the primary groups attempting to expel him from the Conference of Presidents.
He clarifies that the reason for these groups' opposition is his criticism of the Black Lives Matter platform.
He highlights the platform's accusations of Israeli apartheid and genocide as justification for his condemnation.
Klein argues that the BLM platform advocates for the dismantling of key American institutions like the police, military, capitalism, and the nuclear family.
He points out the hypocrisy of those who condemn him as racist for criticizing BLM while simultaneously supporting BLM's anti-Israel stance.
He reveals the Palestinian Authority's 'pay-to-slay' policy rewarding the murder of Jews.
Klein laments the shift of even traditionally pro-Israel Democrats towards anti-Israel positions, citing their support for a Palestinian state and the Iran deal.
He invokes Winston Churchill's famous warning against appeasing the crocodile.
